summary: Lincoln sprawls across nearly 25 square miles of western Placer County foothill terrain — a surprisingly large footprint for a city of about 54,000 — which means much of the landscape is master-planned subdivisions interspersed with rolling grassland, oak-studded ridgelines, and the occasional cattle fence, giving the eastern edges a genuinely rural horizon even as rooftops multiply. The home price-to-income ratio sits around 5.8, which is demanding but notably more accessible than much of the Sacramento metro, and the $108K median household income reflects that this is overwhelmingly a commuter economy: there is no single dominant employer campus in town, and most working residents drive west toward Roseville or south toward Sacramento along Highway 65, a corridor that has become synonymous with stop-and-go congestion during peak hours. Summer highs regularly push into the 90s and triple digits, but with 9.3 hours of average daily sunshine and dry heat rather than humidity, evenings cool meaningfully — the low 50s at night year-round make post-sunset walks along the city's trail network genuinely pleasant. Property crime runs about 689 per 100K, with larceny comprising the bulk, while violent crime registers well below state averages. Lincoln is a place that trades urban convenience and employment density for space, sky, and a mortgage that doesn't require two six-figure incomes — though the price of that bargain is measured in windshield time.
